findings.summary: The artwork-stage version guard is a success-but-stale path that leaves a narrow unfixed F6 window; it is correctly excluded by ADR-023 but is not registered in the limitations register and should be handled by 19.5.
findings.detail: ArtworkPublishingWorkItemProcessor.ProcessAsync (line 80: snapshot.ConfigurationVersion != item.ConfigurationVersion) returns reconciliation.ProcessingResult, i.e. the successful metadata-publication result, without artwork work. It is therefore not a discard and carries no DiscardReason, and the worker does not re-enqueue for it. ADR-023 clause 1 scopes ConfigurationStale to discards (the initial version check and the pre-publication re-check) and the rejected alternative explicitly forbids extending re-enqueue to successful-but-stale work, so the reading in the worker's interpretations[1] is faithful to the accepted decision. The residual operator-visible window is: a save lands after the metadata pre-publication re-check passed but before the artwork-stage version guard, so the item's post-save hint was coalesced, metadata is published under the pre-save version, artwork is skipped, and the pass returns success with no re-enqueue. This is the same F6 symptom (item in flight at save time not re-rendered by the save) in a narrower window, and it is unchanged from before the task. The worker recorded it in worker-report.known_limitations but task 19.5 owns the F6 limitation resolution and the current-state surfaces (docs/limitations/open.md and docs/architecture/08-reconciliation-and-update-flow.md) still describe F6 as open. This does not block 19.3: the v1.2/PLANS F6 acceptance criteria are phrased around a work item that 'discards with the ConfigurationStale classification', which is satisfied, and ADR-023 deliberately excludes successful-but-stale work. Recommended at 19.5: either register this residual (extend F6 or a new bounded ID) or explicitly document it as an accepted residual with the ADR-023 scope rationale so the F6 resolution is not an overclaim.

findings.detail: All 12 MetadataReconciliationProcessor discard sites carry a bounded DiscardReason (verified by grep and source inspection). Direct tests assert the initial ConfigurationStale, ItemMissing, Ineligible, ConnectionChanged, and IdentityUnavailable sites and the pre-publication ConfigurationStale, ItemMissing, and subject-mismatch IdentityUnavailable sites. The provider-kind site (MetadataReconciliationProcessor.cs:132-136) maps to Ineligible by inspection and is unreachable for supported identities (Series/Season fail badge-surface eligibility first), and the pre-publication TryCreate/IsEligible/ConnectionChanged sites map by inspection. Only ConfigurationStale affects worker behavior, so this is diagnostic-only and the acceptance criterion 'all relevant discard sites carry the correct classification' is met; 19.4's coalescing coverage matrix is the appropriate place for broader coverage.
